question.problem: Find the equation of the tangent hyperplane to the hypersurface $w=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2})$ at the point $(1,-1,1,0).$
question.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the hypersurface $w=f(x,y,z)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0},{w}_{0})$ on the hypersurface can be written as

$$
w-{w}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(z-{z}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂z}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}))=\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}))=\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}))=-\frac{2z}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y,z)=(1,-1,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,-1,1) & =\frac{2(1)}{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}-(1)^{2}}=2 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,-1,1) & =\frac{2(-1)}{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}-(1)^{2}}=-2 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z}(1,-1,1) & =-\frac{2(1)}{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}-(1)^{2}}=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent hyperplane:

$$
\begin{aligned}w-0 & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,-1,1)+(y+1)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,-1,1)+(z-1)\frac{∂f}{∂z}(1,-1,1) \\ w & =2(x-1)-2(y+1)-2(z-1) \\ w & =2x-2-2y-2-2z+2 \\ -2x+2y+2z+w+2 & =0 \\ 2x-2y-2z-w-2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
